Closes #38.

pi-action no longer installs `commit-msg` or `prepare-commit-msg` hooks in the target repository. Commit conventions are the repository's job: its own hooks, CI checks, and `AGENTS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Changes

- **`feat: stop installing git hooks in the target repository`**
  - Removes the "Install pi-agent git hooks" step from `action.yml`, and deletes `scripts/install-agent-hooks.js` and `scripts/hooks.test.js`.
  - `scripts/prepare-commit-msg.js` stays. It is this repository's own prek hook, not the injected one, so its tests move to `scripts/prepare-commit-msg.test.js`. Because of it, the `scripts/*.js` knip entries and the vitest `scripts/**/*.test.js` include are still needed, so they stay.
  - New tests:
    - `src/entrypoints.test.ts`: `action.yml` runs only `src/index.ts` and `src/push.ts`, and its `runs:` section never mentions hooks, `core.hooksPath` or `--git-path`.
    - `src/run.test.ts`: on a checkout with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a run where pi commits `release: v0.35.1` (the cv/pit#353 case) leaves `.git/hooks` as it was (only `*.sample`), creates no `.githooks/`, leaves the working tree clean, and keeps the commit message unchanged (no `Refs #…`).
- **`docs: …`**: README feature bullet and docs table, `docs/how-it-works.md` (removes the hooks step and the "Git hooks for the agent" section, adds a "Commit conventions" section), CONTRIBUTING (drops the links to the agent hooks and the file-table row). There was no "step 4 of How It Works" or "line ~167 bullet" in the current files; these are the places that actually described the agent hooks.
- **`docs: add AGENTS.md …`**: a short root `AGENTS.md` that points to CONTRIBUTING's commit messages, `npm run check`, and the documentation style. `src/docs.test.ts` now checks its links too.

`npm run check` (typecheck, lint, coverage, knip/jscpd) passes.

## ⚠️ Needs a maintainer: the commitlint CI job

My token can't push to `.github/workflows/` (`refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow … without workflows permission`), so the CI commit isn't on this branch. Here it is as a patch. Apply it with `git am` before merging:

```bash
gh pr checkout <this PR> && curl -sL <raw patch below> | git am   # or paste it into a file and `git am` it
git push
```

It adds a `commitlint` job to `ci.yml` (pull requests only) that runs `npx --no -- commitlint --from $BASE_SHA --to $HEAD_SHA --verbose` with the existing `commitlint.config.js`. It also adds the matching row in CONTRIBUTING and the line in AGENTS.md, and removes `@commitlint/cli` from knip's `ignoreDependencies` (knip sees it used now, and `--treat-config-hints-as-errors` would fail otherwise). Local checks with the patch applied:
- `npm run check` passes.
- The range of this PR's commits passes commitlint with 0 problems and 0 warnings.
- The same range plus a `release: v0.35.1` commit fails (exit 1, `type-enum`).

PATCH_PLACEHOLDER
```

## Release notes (proposed for v2.3.0)

> ### Changed
> - **pi-action no longer installs git hooks** (#38). Before this release, the action installed a `commit-msg` hook (Conventional Commits only) and a `prepare-commit-msg` hook (`Refs #<first number in the branch name>`) in your checkout. Now pi follows your repository's own conventions: your git hooks, `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. If you want a commit format, enforce it yourself, for example with commitlint in CI (hooks can be skipped with `--no-verify`).

## Open question: version

I went with a **minor** release (2.3.0), and the main commit is `feat:`. No input or output changes. Workflows keep working, and the only difference is that commits that the old hook would have rejected now go through. Nobody should depend on the hooks, so the changelog line above should be enough. I didn't bump `package.json`, because CONTRIBUTING has releases as their own `chore: release` commit.

## Possible follow-up (not in this PR)

pi-action doesn't put `AGENTS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` into the prompt, and pi-durable doesn't load them on its own. pi only finds them when it explores the repository with its tools, and the docs are worded to match. A line in the built-in requirements block ("follow the repository's AGENTS.md / CONTRIBUTING.md when committing") would make that more reliable. That changes the prompt, so I left it out here.
